*   Reduces the number of duplicated Gaussians significantly.
On the Bicycle scene at native resolution with $16 \times 16$ tiles, original AABBs resulted in 87,067,709 duplicated Gaussians.
Using opacity-sensitive ellipses with square boxes reduced this to 55,648,264.
*   **Limitations:** Exact pixel-perfect intersections would result in only 10,976,269 duplicated Gaussians, but are computationally too expensive.
*   Use when rendering large scenes with many transparent or large Gaussians where false-positive tile intersections dominate overhead.
*   Use when memory bandwidth is a bottleneck due to duplicate splat processing.
*   Not necessary for very small scenes or when the overhead of computing the elliptical bounding box outweighs the benefits.
*   If exact pixel-perfect rendering is required and computational resources allow for expensive intersection tests.
Originated from improvements to 3D Gaussian Splatting rendering.
The method was introduced to address the inefficiency of the original 3DGS method, which used circular bounding boxes leading to square AABBs and excessive duplicate splat processing.
